To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antidiuretic and sodium-retaining hormones interact with each other in the kidney, and that this interaction is responsible for some of the previously unexplained phenomena of kidney physiology.
the antidiuretic hormone (ADH), vasopressin, and the sodium retaining hormone (SRH), aldosterone, are both involved in the regulation of water and electrolyte balance in the kidney.
the kidney can be considered as a two compartment system with a high and a low capacity compartment, the latter being a function of the high capacity compartment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction of ADH and Na-retaining hormones in the kidney.
the development of a mathematical model for the kidney.

the development of a theoretical model of the kidney, based on a combination of the two main hypotheses concerning renal function, the hypothesis of antidiurectic hormone (ADH) and the hypothesis of sodium retaining hormones (SRH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) and the sodium-retaining hormone (aldosterone) are antagonistically interacting in the kidney.
the kidney has a very high capacity for the reabsorption of sodium and water and that it is the only organ which has the capacity for the regulation of the sodium balance and the water balance.

the antidiuretic hormone, vasopressin, and the natriumretaining hormones, aldosterone and angiotensin, interact in the kidney to produce a diuresis or an antidiuresis, depending upon which hormone is dominant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antidiuretic and sodium retaining hormones are not antagonistic but are complementary to each other, and that the antidiuresis and natriuresis are two different aspects of the same process, the regulation of the water and salt content of the body fluids.
we have developed an hypothesis for a mechanism of sodium retention in the kidney.
we have developed a theory of the renal function which shows the interrelation of antidiuretically acting hormones and sodium retaining factors in the kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interaction between ADH and Na+ retention hormones is a key determinant of renal water and sodium handling, and that this interaction can explain many of the paradoxical observations in the physiology and pathophysiology of water and salt balance.
there is a fundamental difference between the way that hormones regulate the kidney’s excretion and the way hormones regulate the kidney to conserve salt and water.
we have developed a theoretical framework to explain the interaction between antidiuretic and sodium retaining hormones.
